name: Martin's Corner
why_it_matters: Carafina Pereira opened this four-table corner shop in Betalbatim village in 1989, the year her husband Martin retired. Three decades later it seats 280, serves the king crab Sachin Tendulkar drives down for, and is the South Goa Goan restaurant the rest are measured against.
insider_tip: Live music nightly and Sunday afternoons; book ahead in season (Nov–Jan), the courtyard fills with families. The crab is sized to share — order one between two and add prawn balchão.

name: Zeebop by the Sea
why_it_matters: Sergio Dias has run this open-air seafood shack on Utorda's sand dunes since 1992, sandwiched between Park Hyatt and Kenilworth. Catch comes from boats that morning — kingfish, prawn, crab — grilled over coals at the beach edge.
insider_tip: Sunset table on the sand books out from 5pm; lunch is the easier slot. Open during the monsoon (June–Sep) when most Utorda shacks pull down — Zeebop's permanent structure stays.

name: Chef Fernando's Nostalgia
why_it_matters: Chef Fernando da Costa opened Nostalgia in a restored old Goan house in sleepy Raia village; after his passing, his wife Margarida Tavora e Costa kept the kitchen alive. Times Food Awards named it Best Goan-Portuguese restaurant in 2012, and it remains the south's deepest Goan-Portuguese menu — feijoada, caldinho, serradura — done from family recipes.
insider_tip: Empty old liquor bottles and Goan cooking vessels are the décor; the live folk music at dinner is genuine, not staged. Call ahead — phones are answered, and they'll happily set aside a table on the verandah.

name: Longuinhos Bar, Restaurant & Confectioners
why_it_matters: Jose Pedro Longuinho Almeida Coutinho bought Casa Portuguesa on 1 May 1950 and turned it into Margao's living room. Sons Ilio and Ivo run it now and bake their own bread daily — one of the few Goan kitchens that still does. After liberation it became the South Goan elite's haunt; today office crowds, tourists and old-timers share the same heritage room.
insider_tip: It's a bakery + bar + restaurant rolled into one — duck in for chai and rissois mid-shopping, or settle in for a long Goan lunch. Opposite the Municipality Office, easy walk from Margao station and the Saturday market.
signature_address: Antonio Dias Building, Luis Miranda Road, opposite Municipality Office, Margao, Goa 403601

name: Casa Sarita
why_it_matters: Park Hyatt's signature Goan room, named for the cook who fed the resort's first staff. The interactive show kitchen is lined with home-made pickles and the windows are studded with mother-of-pearl in the colonial Indo-Portuguese style. Three-time Times Food Award winner for Best Goan (2010, 2011, 2012) — the rare upscale restaurant that doesn't treat Goan food as fusion.
insider_tip: Dinner only. Cooking classes with the chef run on request — book through Park Hyatt concierge. Non-residents are welcome; mention you're dining at Casa Sarita to clear the resort gate.
signature_address: Park Hyatt Goa Resort & Spa, Arossim Beach, Cansaulim, Goa 403712

name: Cafe Inn
why_it_matters: Off the main road behind Palolem's rickshaw stand, Cafe Inn grinds its own beans and has been the Palolem long-stay traveller's anchor for nearly two decades. The Lonely Planet listed it as the best breakfast in town years ago and it has held that title through Palolem's many shack cycles.
insider_tip: Palolem's beach shacks tear down 1 May for monsoon and rebuild Oct/Nov — Cafe Inn is one of the few permanent kitchens that stays open year-round, including the wet season. Free Wi-Fi, board games, slow mornings; come for breakfast, stay till lunch.
signature_address: Main Road, behind rickshaw stand, Palolem Beach, Canacona, Goa 403702
